note: Companion to the PR #248 description. Every value here is also stated in the PR text; this file exists so the numbers are machine-readable and citable from a commit instead of from a description that can be edited. Paths are placeholders: the concrete locations are in the private run record, not in the public repo.

configuration.data: 20K listwise subset (residual_train_20000) for the component profile; canonical 185,321-row selection for the steady-state arms

components_ms_per_item.basis: same 8 listwise items, same split, one device
components_ms_per_item.caveat: Means include cold-bucket items. The frozen mean contains one 1.66 s cold-bucket item; the fast-item floor is about 101 ms. The LoRA-before and LoRA-after means likewise include cold-bucket items; the LoRA-after fast-item floor is about 55 ms. The frozen backward is 2 ms because the backbone is frozen, which is the structural half of the gap.
components_ms_per_item.reading: A component decomposition, not a throughput headline. The like-for-like per-item change is 2111 to 994 ms (2.1x).

throughput_points.name: controlled_ab_without_fix_window_1000_1200
throughput_points.source: run of the tree that predates 7bcff68
throughput_points.caveat: Not arranged as a throughput measurement; stopped for unrelated reasons.

throughput_points.name: controlled_ab_with_fix_window_1000_1200
throughput_points.caveat: Same window, same host, same corpus, same selection and seed as the point above.

throughput_points.name: ladder_steady_state_nominal
throughput_points.population: canonical selection, six ladder arms, trained-type rows
throughput_points.source: six LoRA arms of the #233 ladder

validation_rate.purpose: sources the validation term of the per-epoch estimate, which was previously stated at 4.9 items/s with no measurement behind it

code.tree_note: Exported with git archive from the branch tip, so the three hashes above are the branch's own files, not a working copy.

validation_rate.method: Two timed runs of the same command on the same device: --limit 100 and --limit 2100. The 100-item run pays the model load; the difference between the two wall times is the steady-state cost of exactly items 101 to 2100. A repeat of the 2100 run gives the spread.

window.note: Noul rows take the base distribution and never enter the model, so an all-rows rate hides the real cost driver. Choice uses 4 shifts, score 1.

per_epoch_projection.caveat: The noul share is taken from the training mix (85,726 of 185,321 rows) and the rate is measured on the held-out shards, not on the internal split. Both are stated assumptions, not measurements of the internal split.

validation_rate.what_this_replaces: The 4.9 items/s figure in the per-epoch section had no measurement behind it; no file on the compute host or in the repo contained it. The measured value is 5.05 to 5.07 all-rows/s, or 2.65 to 2.66 per model-scored row. The resulting one-device epoch is about 2.7 h of validation, so the 5.0 h estimate is unchanged in substance; the rate and its denominator are now sourced.
